title: After 750 hours and 6 months of non-stop work, I'm finally ready to reveal my Pathfinder 2e Tactics RPG "The Shattered Isles"! I'm happy to talk about my workflow in this thread, and what I did to get this game coherent! (Non-programmer, 5 months, ~4,800 commits: my AI workflow)
author: CrusherEAGLE
selftext:
[https://www.youtube.com/@LunaticDiceGames](https://www.youtube.com/@LunaticDiceGames)

That's my YouTube channel if you'd like to see future devlogs and updates.

*NOTE: I had my Claude Code make a short summary of what my workflow is since it knows it better than I do, but I curated it and made sure it was useful and, well, my edits!*

Hey all. I run Pathfinder 2e games for a living and I can’t code. Since May I’ve been building **The Shattered Isles**, a turn-based tactics game that runs the real PF2e rules, almost entirely with AI. The video of what I made is above. Here’s how I work.

**Code**

* Godot 4.6 with C#. I don’t read the code. I describe what I want in plain English and judge it by playing it.
* Claude Code (Opus 5.5) is the director. It plans, asks me questions, writes the briefs for the workers and reads the finished code.
* Codex (GPT) workers do most of the building. The model that wrote something never reviews it; a different one always checks it.
* The project’s rulebook file is the most important file in the repo. When the AI makes the same mistake twice, the mistake gets a rule or a little guard script that blocks it.
* Every rule is checked against the live Archives of Nethys (the rulebook) page before it ships. Nothing from memory.
* Tests run every night, so the day is just building and playing.

**Art and sound**

* Sprites and animations: PixelLab
* Music: Suno
* Voices: ElevenLabs

**What I’ve learned**

* The AI doesn’t have taste. You do. I make every looks, gameplay, design, and feel call myself.
* Make it ask you questions before it builds. Most of my bad builds came from it guessing what I meant. Seriously, Claude is an idiot if you let it make decisions.
* Build in small chunks you can play in one sitting. ALWAYS playtest a change, no matter how minor, before implementing, or it WILL bite you.
* Write your decisions down in files, so the next chat doesn’t re-ask them or undo them. I have an extensive document tree, almost like the bones of this project.

About 4,800 commits in, and still a lot to do. Happy to answer questions about any of it. I'm not super technical so Claude may respond in my behalf, with me editing.
